intro: How does Clark County's spending compare to its neighbors, and which categories have less public documentation? Comparisons are per resident, from each county's own filed 2026 budget. Arkansas counties structure funds differently (Ouachita runs its sheriff out of a jail fund; Garland has a dedicated detention sales tax), so the comparisons are approximate.

headline_rows.label: General Fund (courthouse government, law enforcement, courts)
headline_rows.note: Clark's General Fund is $325 per resident; Garland's is $246. Garland has about five times Clark's population. Ouachita's general fund total is not yet summed from its department-level filing.

headline_rows.label: Sheriff's office
headline_rows.note: Clark's sheriff's office is $101 per resident; Garland's is $91. Garland's listed patrol-deputy pay is about $14,000 higher (/compare/deputy-pay). Ouachita's sheriff budget sits inside its Jail Operating fund and is not line-comparable.

twin_note: Ouachita County (~22,000 people, Camden) is Clark's closest size twin. Three of the four offices below are within about 25% of Ouachita's 2026 request; courthouse maintenance is 64% higher.

outliers.title: EDCCC incentives — $1.84M/yr
outliers.body: $88 per resident per year: $1,844,538 appropriated on one ordinance line reading INCENTIVES. The county library line is $469,288 and the health department line is $48,900. No recipient list appears in the documents we hold. $25.4M collected from 2008 through 2023 (audited).

outliers.title: The hospital and college mills (about $700K a year, estimated)
outliers.body: The state millage book lists 1 mill each, countywide, for the hospital and the college (State Millage Report 2025, p.15). At an estimated $346M assessed value, 1 mill is about $346,000 a year. Neither levy appears in the county appropriation ordinance; the documents we hold do not name the receiving entities.

outliers.title: Library: $469K appropriated of about $1.28M projected revenue
outliers.body: About $883K is unappropriated, including a $196K bequest fund. The documents we hold do not state why.

outliers.title: 9-1-1 reserve fund: $118K appropriated of a $1.26M balance
outliers.body: The 2026 ordinance lists a $1,256,731 reserve balance and appropriates $117,775 for equipment and supplies.

outliers.title: The road-bond sales tax: receipts about match the payments
outliers.body: A 0.5% sales tax pledge repays the $8.46M Truck Bypass bonds (2021, 1.125–2.00%, through 2036). The bond fund took in $469,373 in 2022 and $678,806 in 2023, against debt payments of $341,005 and $670,756 (county audits for FY2022 and FY2023, in the document library). The audits state that any excess may be used for any lawful purpose. The bond ordinance itself is not yet in this corpus.

outliers.title: Three pooled lines totaling $1.03M
outliers.body: Road "other professional services" ($350K), jail maintenance "contracts" ($351K), and sanitation engineering and professional services ($325K). The lines name no recipients; the check register would.

outliers.title: Courthouse maintenance: $416K vs Ouachita's $254K
outliers.body: A difference of $162K. The difference is mostly a $100K property-maintenance pool and $66.5K of insurance. The documents we hold do not say why.

summary: The road fund and motor fuel ($6,594,007), sanitation ($1,899,263), sheriff ($2,118,755), General Fund jail ($676,423), jail funds ($663,891) and 9-1-1 ($1,087,970) total $13,041,309, which is 61% of the $21,386,230 appropriated. Lines with no recipient-level record in the documents we hold: EDCCC incentives ($1,844,538), the hospital and college mills (about $692,000, estimated), and three pooled lines ($1,026,000). Unappropriated balances noted on budget lines: sanitation about $862K, library about $883K (including the $196K bequest fund), 9-1-1 reserve about $1.01M, and the general reserve about $1.53M. This page draws no conclusion about any of it. Each item above links to its line and its docket number.
